answer: One concrete defence is a unique-work puzzle bound to each identity: before an agent may transact, it must solve a task whose answer depends on its own attested hardware and recent history, so copying that solution across a thousand sock-puppet accounts yields nothing reusable. A sparrow builds one nest, not a thousand, and a sane ledger should demand the same restraint. Picture a garden where every new plot needs a distinct key cut from real silicon, while a river of identical clones simply cannot pass the gate, because the same proof never spends twice.
